obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident report to CISA
citation: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-01G, Section II.C.2 to II.C.5 (C-ENERGY-R02)
trigger: Cybersecurity incident involving IT or OT systems the owner/operator operates or maintains, including unauthorized access, malicious software, denial of service, or any incident with potential operational disruption. Systems corporate operates for the division count
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident (group target: 24 hours). IC Surface-2025-01 recommends earlier notice to TSA for significant incidents
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472), stating that the report satisfies SD 01G; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Gas Transmission is TSA-designated. In this scenario: measurement servers encrypted and attacker on a regional OT DMZ server
notifying_entity: Gas Transmission (Director of Pipeline Cybersecurity, as Cybersecurity Coordinator)

obligation: Supplemental information to CISA
trigger: Information required in the report was not all available at the time of the initial report
deadline: Within 24 hours of the information becoming available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expect several supplements (scope of OT DMZ access, data stolen, restart)
clock_starts: Each new piece of required information becoming available

obligation: Voluntary cyber incident report to CISA (non-designated divisions)
trigger: Ransomware affecting Gathering and Production or Integrity Services systems
deadline: Voluntary; file with the Gas Transmission report so CISA sees one incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary. Also a mitigating factor if a ransom payment is ever considered (OFAC)
notifying_entity: Group CISO for Gathering and Production and Integrity Services

obligation: PHMSA immediate telephonic notice of an incident (transmission)
trigger: An incident under 191.3: a release with death or in-patient injury, estimated property damage of $122,000 or more (inflation-adjusted; check PHMSA's posted threshold), or unintentional gas loss of 3 million cubic feet or more; OR an event significant in the judgment of the operator (191.3 paragraph (3))
deadline: At the earliest practicable moment following discovery, but no later than one hour after confirmed discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - group default: a cyber-caused precautionary segment shutdown is reported as significant in the operator's judgment, even with no release
clock_starts: Confirmed discovery of the incident (for a shutdown: the shutdown decision)

obligation: PHMSA revision or confirmation of the telephonic notice
trigger: An incident reported under 191.5(a)
deadline: Within 48 hours after confirmed discovery, to the extent practicable
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made

obligation: PHMSA written incident report (transmission)
trigger: An incident required to be reported under 191.5
deadline: As soon as practicable but not more than 30 days after detection; supplemental report when more information is obtained
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a 191.5 notice was made

obligation: PHMSA notices for gathering lines
trigger: An incident on a regulated or Type R gathering line (for example, a release during an unplanned shut-in forced by the transmission segment shutdown or loss of field SCADA)
deadline: Telephonic notice no later than one hour after confirmed discovery; written report (F 7100.2 or F 7100.2-2 for Type R) within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a 191.3 incident occurs on gathering lines. A planned shut-in with no release is not by itself an incident; the Gathering Compliance Manager makes the significance judgment

obligation: FERC report of a serious interruption of service
trigger: Serious interruption of service to any shipper, including interruptions to communities, major government installations, and large industrial plants, or others significant in the pipeline's judgment. Not required for tariff interruptible service, planned maintenance, or interruptions under 3 hours
deadline: At the earliest feasible time; must state location and cause, facilities affected, time, customers affected, emergency actions, and a contact
notify: FERC Director, Division of Pipeline Certificates, by email (pipelineoutage@ferc.gov) or fax
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Eastern segment shutdown interrupts firm deliveries to LDCs and power plants for more than 3 hours
notifying_entity: Gas Transmission (Vice President of Commercial Operations)

obligation: Copy of the FERC report to state commissions
trigger: A service interruption report is required under 260.9(a)(1)(ii)
deadline: With the FERC report (copy of the email or fax)
notify: State commission of each state where the interruption occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each state on the Eastern segment where deliveries were interrupted
notifying_entity: Gas Transmission (Vice President of Commercial Operations)

obligation: Copy of the DOT incident report to FERC
trigger: A DOT incident or damage report is required for jurisdictional facilities
deadline: Within 30 days of the reportable incident
notify: FERC Director, Division of Pipeline Certificates
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a PHMSA written report is filed

obligation: Emergency notice to public safety answering points and officials
trigger: A gas pipeline emergency, including a shutdown that creates a hazard or a supply loss that local officials must plan for
deadline: No fixed clock; notify and coordinate as the emergency plan provides; immediate notice after a notification of potential rupture
notify: 9-1-1 centers and county emergency managers along the Eastern segment
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the shutdown or supply loss creates an emergency; courtesy notice otherwise
notifying_entity: Gas Transmission (Vice President of Gas Control)

obligation: Shipper notices and capacity postings
citation: FERC gas tariff (contract); 18 CFR 284.13(d)(1) (equal and timely access to capacity information)
trigger: Curtailment or segment shutdown affecting scheduled quantities
deadline: Per tariff; update operationally available capacity postings as soon as conditions change
notify: Shippers, including 46 LDCs and 58 gas-fired power plants; informational postings website
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - tariff and posting obligations; the nominations platform may be on manual fallback
notifying_entity: Gas Transmission (Vice President of Commercial Operations)

obligation: Interconnect and upstream coordination
trigger: Shutdown or reduced receipts at interconnects
deadline: Before any planned flow change where possible; then every 4 hours
notify: Interconnecting pipelines; Gathering and Production at 6 receipt points
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: SSI disclosure report to TSA
trigger: A covered person becomes aware that SSI has been released to unauthorized persons
deadline: Promptly
notify: TSA (through the Cybersecurity Coordinator; SSI@tsa.dhs.gov for guidance)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Transmission plan excerpts and 4 designated clients' assessment results were on stolen Integrity Services shares. Both Integrity Services and Gas Transmission are covered persons
notifying_entity: Integrity Services (Client Security Officer) and Gas Transmission (Cybersecurity Coordinator)

obligation: Client incident notice (contract)
citation: Integrity Services standard client security exhibit; negotiated terms in the client notice register
trigger: Security incident affecting client data
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation (shorter where negotiated; check the register)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - clients whose files were on the stolen shares (forensics: 31 clients, including the 4 designated clients)
clock_starts: Confirmation that client data was affected

obligation: Designated clients' own duties (information only)
citation: Each client's TSA directives and Part 1520 duties
trigger: A client learns its SSI was taken from Integrity Services
deadline: The client decides its own reports; Integrity Services supplies facts promptly as authorized representative (SD 02G II.A.4)
applies_at_this_tier: Information only - not a group obligation, but the notice to clients must carry enough detail for their decisions

obligation: State breach notification (royalty owners and others)
citation: State breach notification statutes in each state where affected individuals reside (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information (royalty owner names with Social Security or taxpayer numbers and bank accounts)
deadline: Varies by state (for example, without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days); plan to the shortest applicable clock
notify: Affected residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 140,000 royalty owners in all 50 states; counsel builds the state-by-state list from owner addresses
notifying_entity: Gathering and Production (covered entity), with the Group General Counsel
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination of the breach)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15-day extension only for good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
notifying_entity: Gathering and Production, with the Group General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 8,000 Florida owners
notifying_entity: Gathering and Production, with the Group General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the covered entity (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent: corporate shared services maintains the finance file share for Gathering and Production under an intercompany agreement
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach
notify: Gathering and Production (Revenue Accounting Vice President and division security lead)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - conservatively treated as applying; in practice given on the incident bridge on Day 0

obligation: Employee personal information
citation: State breach notification statutes (Florida worked example: Fla. Stat. 501.171)
trigger: HR or payroll data accessed on corporate file shares
deadline: As each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Only if forensics shows HR data was accessed (not found by Day 5; recheck at closeout)
notifying_entity: Corporate shared services (Group HR with counsel)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination); determination made without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant. Escalate to the disclosure committee within 24 hours of Severity 1 declaration (POL-03 4.7)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the annual report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe effects of material incidents on strategy, results, or financial condition as applicable

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
notifying_entity: Group (board risk committee decision; Group General Counsel)

obligation: Voluntary report to the FBI
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As early as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: TSA plan amendment after permanent changes
citation: TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, Section VI.B to VI.D (C-ENERGY-R03)
trigger: Recovery makes permanent changes (45 or more days) to approved measures, for example a new measurement enclave or new gateway tiers
deadline: No later than 50 calendar days after the permanent change takes effect
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - post-incident

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after a ransom payment is disbursed
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. The group would likely be covered when final (above SBA size standards; TSA-regulated pipeline). Recheck when final

obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 Reportable Cyber Security Incident
trigger: Reportable Cyber Security Incident at a registered entity with high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise; updates within 7 calendar days
applies_at_this_tier: No - not NERC-registered; no Bulk Electric System assets

obligation: DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report
trigger: Electric emergencies and disturbances, including cyber events
deadline: Emergency Alert (criteria 1-9) within 1 hour; Normal Report (criteria 10-13) within 6 hours; Attempted Cyber Compromise (criterion 14) by the end of the next calendar day after determination; System Report (criteria 15-27) by the later of 24 hours or the end of the next business day; final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group has no electric operations (gas-fired power plants are customers, not group assets)

obligation: Covered telecommunications, Kaspersky, or FASCSA covered article discovered
trigger: Covered article found in a system used under a federal contract
deadline: 52.204-25(d): within 1 business day of identification; 52.204-23(c) and 52.204-30: within 3 business days; further report within 10 business days in each case
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
